holes_found.description: RHETORICAL FRAMING WEAKNESS on Chapel Hill outlier: detail_evidence dismisses Chapel Hill's +0.267° drift as 'consistent with measurement noise and city-centroid choice.' Chapel Hill +0.267° at 35.9°N latitude corresponds to ≈30 km of north-south displacement (latitude-degree ≈ 111 km × 0.267 ≈ 29.6 km). 30 km is well above typical city-centroid uncertainty for an inhabited town (Chapel Hill, NC town extent is ~few km), so the 'city-centroid choice' framing is rhetorically weak — a defender can fairly respond 'Chapel Hill town center is not 30 km uncertain; you're hand-waving the only positive datapoint.' The 'measurement noise' framing is more defensible (single ±0.2–0.5° inclinometer reading), but combining the two as parallel explanations dilutes the stronger argument: even taken AT FACE VALUE, +0.267° is 5×–25× SMALLER than PRED-NEW-001's predicted +1.4° (Edinburgh) to +5.5° (Helsinki) at >55°N — so Chapel Hill is irrelevant to the registered prediction even if treated as a real signal. The magnitude argument is unimpeachable; the noise argument has a quibble surface.
holes_found.recommendation: One-clause substitution in detail_evidence: replace 'both consistent with measurement noise and city-centroid choice, not with the multi-degree systematic excess PRED-NEW-001 predicts' with 'both consistent with a single ±0.2–0.5° inclinometer reading at the noise level — and even taken at face value, +0.267° remains 5×–25× smaller than the +1.4° to +5.5° multi-degree excess PRED-NEW-001 predicts at >55°N.' This drops the city-centroid quibble surface and foregrounds the unimpeachable magnitude argument. Self-applyable; not blocking the verdict.

advocate_mode.best_defense: Three lines of defense remain: (1) Chapel Hill +0.267° IS a real positive offset (the noise framing concedes this implicitly); the dome's reading at 35.9°N is consistent with a global signal of order 0.25° that scales upward with latitude (linear extrapolation 0.267° × (60/36) ≈ 0.45° at Oslo — still well below PRED-NEW-001's 64.4° prediction, but you cannot dismiss 'a positive offset exists' the way you dismiss zero). (2) The dome's coordinate table that lists Oslo at 59.90° was built BEFORE PRED-NEW-001 was registered (2026-03-12) — the dome may argue the coordinate table uses the WGS84-anchored coordinate system as input convention and the PRED-NEW-001 prediction is what an inclinometer at Oslo would measure, which is a SEPARATE quantity from the table's 'lat'. Your self-contradiction argument depends on equating two values the dome would label differently. (3) PRED-NEW-001 is PENDING (per raw-text/03-predictions.txt) — no Oslo measurement exists yet, so 'refuted by data' is technically premature; the actual test is pending and your case is built on the dome's own contradiction, not on a measurement.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: All three defenses fail on the existing prose: (1) the Chapel Hill linear-extrapolation defense (0.45° at Oslo) is itself an order of magnitude below the dome's own 4.5° prediction — the defender accidentally concedes the prediction is wrong by 10×. (2) The 'separate quantities' defense is at odds with how PRED-NEW-001 is operationally defined in the dome's own raw text ('actual Polaris elevation measured with calibrated inclinometer will be 3-7 deg HIGHER THAN WGS84 latitude' — the dome explicitly contrasts measured-elevation vs WGS84-lat, the same quantities the coordinate table records); proposing that the table uses 'WGS84-anchored coordinates that don't correspond to inclinometer readings' would force the dome to admit its coordinate system is detached from observable measurements, gutting the V12 coordinate system itself. (3) The 'PENDING' defense is weak because the verdict 'Refuted by Data' is anchored by the dome's INTERNAL self-contradiction (table vs PRED-NEW-001 numerics), not by an external measurement — the dome's own published numbers refute the dome's own published prediction. defense_survives drops from 0.5 (concession potential from defense 1) → 0 after the proposed c5 H1 magnitude-argument substitution closes the linear-extrapolation gap explicitly.
